scenes.heading: Selling add-ons and upsells without feeling pushy

sents.d: Selling add-ons and upsells without feeling pushy
The easiest revenue increase is often not a new client, but a bigger order from an existing one.

Add-ons — drone footage, a same-day highlight edit, an extra final format for social media, rush turnaround — are usually easier to sell than the core package itself, because the client has already said yes to working with you.

scenes.heading: Offer them as a menu up front

sents.d: Presenting these as an optional menu at the proposal stage (rather than a hard upsell after booking) removes the pushy feeling entirely: the client sees the options once, picks what fits their budget, and you never have to have an awkward add-on conversation mid-project.
Track which add-ons actually get chosen over a few months — this tells you which ones to keep offering prominently and which to quietly drop, rather than guessing.

take: Show optional add-ons in the proposal, then track what sells.
